rules.summary: zext/sext mult < mult -> (and (not t=0) (not a=0) (= (bv[su]lt (x+t) x) (bvsgt a 0)))
rules.guard_comparison: (i) rewriteViaRule = C++ MultSltMult. extract_ext_tuple (simplification.h:1861) returns (zext-inner, sext-inner, false) for a concat/sext pair, but applies() (:1893) then uses the two inners symmetrically: addxt may be ml[0] or ml[1], and `a` may match mr[0] or mr[1]. Correctness needs addxt = the zero-extended inner on the left AND a = the sign-extended inner on the right. (ii) The elaborator (:300-375) adds RCONS_SIMPLE steps for concat-0 -> zero_extend (reconstructed by bv-zero-extend-eliminate) and for operand swaps chosen by a syntactic heuristic (reconstructed by bv_poly_norm). It then ALWAYS adds a trusted step (:371) `normalized-lhs = C++ rhs` and returns true. That residue is re-proved only by RARE with theory rewrites off (proof_post_processor_dsl.cpp:136). When no RARE rule matches, the trust step stays and states the unsound equality verbatim. (iii) No Eunoia definition: the macro exists only via elaboration. (iv) cvc5_proof_rule.h:3613 defines it as 'rewritten by internal rule MultSltMult', which is circular.
rules.guard_gap: Two independent operand-role cases are accepted by the C++ and match no RARE rule: (A) #13039, where the add is under sign_extend and a under zero_extend on the left; (B) new, where the left is correct but on the right the shared a is zero-extended and x sign-extended, e.g. (bvslt (bvmul (zext (x+t)) (sext a)) (bvmul (zext a) (sext x))). A fix that pins only the left-hand roles leaves (B) open. Sound but unreconstructed: (C) sext/sext where the shared factor is itself an add; the elaborator's swap heuristic keys on 'sext of ADD', swaps the wrong mult, and leaves an RCONS_SIMPLE trust step (z3 agrees it is valid).

rules.summary: x op (concat ys c zs) -> concat of x-slices op parts, for c in {0,1,ones}
rules.guard_comparison: The elaborator only handles a constant strictly inside a concat. It groups that concat as (concat pre c post) through an RCONS_SIMPLE step (:410, ACI_NORM-closable), then ALWAYS adds a trusted residue (:431) expected to be bv-*-concat-pullup3. This is the same shape as MultSltMult (normalize, then trust the remainder). If no concat has a middle constant it returns false (:421), leaving THEORY_REWRITE MACRO_* which prints as trust. C++ picks the FIRST concat child (simplification.h:487), while the elaborator groups EVERY concat child with a middle constant, so with two such children the residue's x differs syntactically from the C++ x. The rewrite is sound for any constant (bitwise ops distribute over concat), so a mismatch costs coverage, not soundness.

rules.dispatch: every BV pre/postRewrite call -> one TRUST_THEORY_REWRITE step -> ProofPostprocessDsl::update -> RewriteDbProofCons::prove
rules.summary: how a hand-written BV step becomes (or fails to become) a checked proof
rules.guard_comparison: Order (rewrite_db_proof_cons.cpp:58-140, basic_rewrite_rcons.cpp:67-140): EVALUATE, DISTINCT_VALUES, PRE_DSL theory rewrites, RARE search (recLimit/stepLimit), retry on the converted form, then POST_DSL theory rewrites. A theory rewrite is selected by findRule, which reruns the C++ (rewriteViaRule) and checks the result is the RHS, so it is circular by construction. A MACRO_BV_* hit is then elaborated (ensureProofForTheoryRewrite). Elaboration subgoals tagged MACRO_THEORY_REWRITE_RCONS_SIMPLE are re-proved by RARE with theory rewrites disabled (proof_post_processor_dsl.cpp:136) and nesting depth < 3. RARE conditions ARE enforced: getObligations evaluates side conditions, each obligation must be proved (proveInternalBase evaluates both sides and FAILs on distinct values, else recursive proof), and the proved conditions become premises of DSL_REWRITE, re-checked by Ethos. BV registers no DSL_SUBCALL theory rewrites, so conditions are never discharged by circular THEORY_REWRITE. So a C++ step that violates a RARE condition cannot be justified by that RARE rule. It ends in one of three visible states: (1) trust MACRO_THEORY_REWRITE_RCONS_SIMPLE, an elaborator residue or normalization step that RARE could not close (the #13039 signature: the trust step states the unsound equation verbatim); (2) trust <macro-id> (e.g. macro-bv-xor-simplify), where the elaborator returned false and the THEORY_REWRITE has no CPC definition (eo_printer.cpp:298 handles only BV_UMULO/SMULO/REPEAT/BITWISE_SLICING); (3) trust TRUST_THEORY_REWRITE, where nothing matched. The hole is policy, not logic: by default cvc5 still answers unsat, prints the trust step and passes --check-proofs (TRUST accepted; THEORY_REWRITE checker circular). --no-proof-allow-trust (cpc printer) and --check-proofs --proof-pedantic=10 abort on the buggy probes, but they also abort on sound-but-unreconstructed steps (MACRO_BV_MULT_SLT_MULT_add_in_both), so a trust step does not by itself distinguish a bug from a coverage gap. Two elaborators end with an unconditional trusted residue and return true: MultSltMult (:371) and AndOrXorConcatPullup (:431). Simplify (:119) is similar but only for the non-constant part. Out of unit: TheoryBV::ppStaticRewrite/ppRewrite (theory_bv.cpp:202-260: UltAddOne, SolveEq, BitwiseEq, Sign/ZeroExtendEqConst) feed steps into the same pipeline.
rules.guard_gap: Any C++ rewrite whose (normalized) form matches no RARE rule becomes an unflagged trust step under default options.
rules.probe_result: unsound steps -> trust MACRO_THEORY_REWRITE_RCONS_SIMPLE; sound uncovered -> same trust id; elaboration failure -> trust macro-bv-xor-simplify
rules.rationale: RARE conditions are enforced, but every uncovered C++ step degrades silently to trust. Unless trust is rejected, soundness of uncovered steps rests on the C++ alone, and trust steps cannot tell bugs from coverage gaps.
